findings.title: Detection rule's file-reading mechanism is unspecified and has no supporting API
findings.description: The design states the new `ConsistencyChecker` rule "scans the shared project file for any key whose `CONFIG_KEYS[key].scope === 'personal'`," but no mechanism is specified and none currently exists. `ConfigManager` exposes no API to enumerate the raw keys present in a *specific* file: `get()` resolves one key through the full precedence chain, and `list()` is built on `get()`, so with the new precedence a personal key present in *both* files resolves as `source: 'project-personal'` and the shared-file copy is invisible. The `readToml` helper that would be needed is module-private and not exported (`packages/core/src/config/ConfigManager.ts`), and the `Component Structure` / `API Contracts` sections add only `getProjectPersonalConfigPath` — no key-enumeration helper. Since the design's own Collision Semantics acknowledge the both-files case exists, the detection rule needs a concrete read API (e.g. an exported per-file key enumerator or a new `ConfigManager` method), and the design should name it. As written, the implementer must invent an unstated cross-layer dependency (reading TOML directly from `introspection/`) to satisfy the rule.

findings.title: "existing config-hygiene-style checks" do not exist in ConsistencyChecker
findings.description: The design says the rule is "added alongside the existing config-hygiene-style checks." No such rule category exists — the current rules are `task-vs-plan`, `frontmatter-vs-computed`, `missing-artifact`, `plan-vs-frontmatter`, `task-file-status`, `review-gate`, `duplicate-index`, `plan-status-vs-entries`, `arch-status-vs-plans`, `initiative-*`, `stale-worktree-path`, and `frontmatter-schema`; the only existing config interaction is `resolveGateConfig()`. The reference could mislead an implementer into looking for a pattern to copy. Minor wording fix.

findings.title: MCP `workflow_check` tool description is not updated for the new rule
findings.description: The design correctly notes the rule "surfaces automatically through ... MCP `workflow_check`," but the `Component Structure` MCP entry lists only `configTools.ts` as changed. `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/workflowTools.ts`'s `workflow_check` description enumerates the categories it detects, so adding a rule leaves that description stale. Either add `workflowTools.ts` to the change list or state explicitly that the description is left as-is.
